resolvedSemantics.objective: Replace every ! with 0 or 1 and minimize the sum over adjacent pairs: 01 costs x, 10 costs y.
resolvedSemantics.evidence: The fixed raw statement explicitly scores every adjacent pair as 01 -> x and 10 -> y, and asks for the minimum after replacing every !. The Python, Java and C++ implementations all perform the same two-state minimum-cost DP. Direct enumeration gives 5 for Example 1 and 3 for Example 2; the published values are not minima.
resolvedSemantics.inputDomain: Raw source: S uses 0, 1, !; length 1..100000; at least one !; x,y are nonnegative integers. The site protocol bounds x,y to nonnegative signed 32-bit values, matching the original Java/C++ int parameters; the answer fits signed 64-bit.
resolvedSemantics.siteProtocol: Line 1: S. Line 2: x y. Output the minimum as an integer. The 32-bit input bound is disclosed as matching the original signatures.
